name: M1A2 Abrams
description: The M1A2 Abrams is the main battle tank of the United States Army, featuring advanced composite armor, a 120mm smoothbore cannon, and a gas-turbine engine.
admin_note: Export variant restrictions apply. Verify FMS documentation.

name: Leopard 2A7
description: The Leopard 2A7 is a third-generation German main battle tank, widely regarded for its firepower, protection, and mobility across NATO forces.

name: T-90M Proryv
description: The T-90M is a modernized Russian main battle tank with the Relikt explosive reactive armor package and an upgraded fire-control system.

name: M2A3 Bradley
armament: 25mm M242 Bushmaster, TOW missile launcher, 7.62mm coax
description: The M2 Bradley is a tracked infantry fighting vehicle that transports a squad while providing fire support with its autocannon and anti-tank missiles.

name: BMP-3
description: The BMP-3 is a Soviet-designed amphibious infantry fighting vehicle with a uniquely heavy mixed-caliber armament package for its class.

name: M1126 Stryker
description: The Stryker is an eight-wheeled armored personnel carrier providing rapid, protected mobility for infantry squads on the modern battlefield.

name: M109A7 Paladin
description: The M109A7 Paladin is a self-propelled 155mm howitzer providing indirect fire support with improved survivability and automated loading.

name: Tiger I
description: The Tiger I was a German heavy tank of World War II, renowned for its powerful 88mm gun and thick frontal armor that dominated early engagements.
admin_note: Historical reference entry — not in active service.

name: Challenger 2
armament: 120mm L30A1 rifled gun, 7.62mm L94A1 chain gun, 7.62mm L37A2 MG
description: The Challenger 2 is the British Army's main battle tank, known for its Dorchester armour and its service in the Balkans and Iraq.

name: Leclerc
armament: 120mm CN120-26/52 smoothbore gun with autoloader, 12.7mm M2HB coax, 7.62mm MG
description: The Leclerc is France's main battle tank, featuring an autoloader that allows a three-person crew and a high-performance hyperbar diesel engine.

name: Merkava Mk 4
description: The Merkava Mk 4 places its engine at the front for extra crew protection and has a rear hatch that can carry infantry or casualties. It is fitted with the Trophy active protection system.

name: K2 Black Panther
armament: 120mm CN08 L/55 smoothbore gun with autoloader, 12.7mm K6, 7.62mm coax
description: The K2 Black Panther is one of the most advanced tanks in service, with hydropneumatic suspension that lets it kneel and tilt to aim over terrain.

name: Type 10
armament: 120mm L/44 smoothbore gun with autoloader, 12.7mm M2, 7.62mm coax
description: The Type 10 is a lightweight Japanese main battle tank with modular ceramic armour and a C4I network system, designed for mobility on Japan's roads and bridges.

name: Type 99A
armament: 125mm ZPT-98 smoothbore gun with autoloader, 12.7mm QJC-88, 7.62mm coax
description: The Type 99A is the most capable main battle tank of the Chinese People's Liberation Army, fitted with composite and reactive armour and a laser warning system.

name: T-14 Armata
description: The T-14 Armata is a Russian tank with an unmanned turret; its crew of three sits in an armoured capsule in the hull. Only a small number have been produced.

name: T-72B3
description: The T-72 is one of the most widely produced tanks in history. The B3 upgrade adds modern thermal sights and a better fire-control system to the 1970s Soviet design.

name: T-80BV
description: The T-80 was the first production tank to use a gas-turbine engine as its main powerplant, giving it high speed at the cost of heavy fuel consumption.

name: T-55
description: The T-54/T-55 series is the most-produced tank family in history, with tens of thousands built and service in more than 50 countries.

name: M60A3 Patton
description: The M60 was the US Army's main battle tank through most of the Cold War; the A3 variant added a laser rangefinder and thermal sights.

name: Leopard 1A5
description: The Leopard 1 put mobility ahead of armour and became one of the most successful Western tanks of the Cold War, exported across Europe and beyond.

name: Chieftain Mk 10
armament: 120mm L11A5 rifled gun, 12.7mm ranging MG, 2x 7.62mm MG
description: The Chieftain was the most heavily armed and armoured tank in NATO when it entered service in the 1960s, and it introduced a reclined driver position.

name: Centurion
description: The Centurion was one of the most successful post-war tank designs, serving in conflicts from Korea to the Middle East for more than 50 years.

name: Arjun Mk 1A
description: The Arjun is India's domestically developed main battle tank; the Mk 1A adds dozens of upgrades to firepower, mobility, and protection.

name: Altay
description: The Altay is Turkey's new-generation main battle tank, developed with South Korean assistance and based on K2 technology.

name: C1 Ariete
description: The Ariete is the Italian Army's main battle tank, built by the Iveco–OTO Melara consortium and in service since 1995.

name: Stridsvagn 122
description: The Stridsvagn 122 is a Swedish Leopard 2 variant with extra armour and a command-and-control system tailored to the Swedish Army.

name: PT-91 Twardy
description: The PT-91 Twardy is a Polish development of the T-72M1, adding ERAWA explosive reactive armour and a modernised fire-control system.

name: T-84 Oplot-M
description: The Oplot-M is Ukraine's most advanced tank, developed from the T-80UD with a welded turret, Duplet reactive armour, and a diesel engine.

name: Al-Khalid
armament: 125mm smoothbore gun with autoloader, 12.7mm AA MG, 7.62mm coax
description: The Al-Khalid was jointly developed by Pakistan and China and serves as a mainstay of the Pakistan Army's armoured corps.

name: M4A3E8 Sherman
description: The M4 Sherman was the most widely used Allied tank of WWII. The "Easy Eight" variant added a longer 76mm gun and horizontal volute spring suspension.

name: T-34-85
description: The T-34 combined sloped armour, a powerful gun, and ease of production. The T-34-85 up-gunned version became the backbone of Soviet armoured forces in 1944–45.

name: Panther Ausf. G
description: The Panther was Germany's answer to the T-34, pairing a high-velocity 75mm gun with thick sloped frontal armour.

name: Panzer IV Ausf. H
description: The Panzer IV was the only German tank to stay in production for the whole war, adapting from infantry support to a capable anti-tank role.

name: Cromwell
description: The Cromwell was one of the fastest tanks of WWII thanks to its Rolls-Royce Meteor engine, derived from the Merlin aero engine.

name: Type 97 Chi-Ha
description: The Type 97 Chi-Ha was the most widely produced Japanese medium tank of WWII, used across China, the Pacific, and Southeast Asia.

name: Tiger II
description: The Tiger II ("King Tiger") combined the long 88mm gun with heavily sloped armour, but its weight made it unreliable and fuel-hungry.

name: IS-2
description: The IS-2 was a Soviet breakthrough tank whose 122mm gun was designed to knock out fortifications and German heavy tanks alike.

name: KV-1
description: The KV-1 was nearly immune to German anti-tank guns in 1941, and a single KV could hold up entire columns during the early months of Operation Barbarossa.

name: Churchill Mk VII
description: The Churchill was a heavily armoured British infantry tank that could climb steep terrain, and it formed the basis of many specialist engineering vehicles.

name: M26 Pershing
description: The M26 Pershing arrived in the last months of WWII and became the basis for the US Patton tank series.

name: M24 Chaffee
description: The M24 Chaffee replaced the M3/M5 Stuart, adding a 75mm gun while keeping the speed a reconnaissance tank needs.

name: M3 Stuart
description: The M3 Stuart was a fast, reliable light tank supplied to Allied forces around the world. British crews nicknamed it the "Honey".

name: PT-76
description: The PT-76 is an amphibious light tank that swims with water jets. It saw action from Vietnam to the Indo-Pakistani wars.

name: M551 Sheridan
description: The M551 Sheridan was an air-droppable light tank whose 152mm gun could fire both conventional shells and guided missiles.

name: FV101 Scorpion
description: The Scorpion holds the record as the fastest production tank. It was light enough to be airlifted and used aluminium armour.

name: ZTQ-15
description: The ZTQ-15 (Type 15) light tank was designed for high-altitude and rugged terrain such as the Tibetan Plateau, where heavy tanks struggle.

name: M10 Booker
description: The M10 Booker was a US Army infantry-support vehicle developed under the Mobile Protected Firepower program. The Army cancelled it in 2025.

name: Jagdpanther
description: The Jagdpanther mounted the Tiger II's 88mm gun on a Panther chassis and is often regarded as one of the best tank destroyers of the war.

name: StuG III Ausf. G
description: The StuG III was Germany's most-produced fully tracked armoured fighting vehicle of WWII. Its low profile made it an effective assault gun and tank hunter.

name: M18 Hellcat
description: The M18 Hellcat was the fastest tracked armoured vehicle of WWII, sacrificing armour for speed and ambush tactics.

name: SU-100
description: The SU-100 put a powerful 100mm gun on the T-34 chassis and remained in service with some armies decades after WWII.

name: B1 Centauro
description: The Centauro is an eight-wheeled tank destroyer that pioneered the concept of a wheeled vehicle carrying a tank-calibre gun.

name: 2S25 Sprut-SD
description: The Sprut-SD is an amphibious, air-droppable tank destroyer for Russian airborne forces, armed with a full-size 125mm tank gun.

name: CV90
description: The CV90 family was designed for Nordic winters and is now operated by many European armies in a wide range of variants.

name: Puma
description: The Puma is one of the most heavily protected infantry fighting vehicles in the world, with modular armour packages and a remote-controlled turret.

name: Marder 1A3
description: The Marder was the first infantry fighting vehicle fielded by a NATO army and served the Bundeswehr for five decades.

name: FV510 Warrior
armament: 30mm L21A1 RARDEN cannon, 7.62mm L94A1 chain gun
description: The Warrior has been the British Army's tracked infantry fighting vehicle since 1988 and saw extensive service in the Gulf, the Balkans, and Iraq.

name: BMP-1
description: The BMP-1 was the world's first mass-produced infantry fighting vehicle. It let troops fight from inside the vehicle under armour.

name: BMP-2
description: The BMP-2 replaced its predecessor's low-pressure gun with a rapid-fire 30mm autocannon that can engage helicopters and light vehicles.

name: VBCI
description: The VBCI is a French eight-wheeled infantry fighting vehicle built for strategic mobility, and it has been deployed to Mali and Lebanon.

name: K21
description: The K21 uses a composite hull to stay light enough to swim while carrying a powerful 40mm gun.

name: ZBD-04A
description: The ZBD-04 is a Chinese amphibious infantry fighting vehicle whose turret layout is inspired by the BMP-3.

name: BMD-4M
description: The BMD-4M is an air-droppable infantry fighting vehicle for Russian airborne troops, sharing the BMP-3's heavy turret.

name: Lynx KF41
armament: 30mm or 35mm Wotan autocannon, 7.62mm coax, Spike-LR ATGM
description: The Rheinmetall Lynx is a modular infantry fighting vehicle chosen by Hungary and Italy, built to be reconfigured for different missions.

name: M113
description: The M113 is the most widely used armoured fighting vehicle family ever, with more than 80,000 built in dozens of variants. The Philippine Army also operates it.

name: BTR-80
description: The BTR-80 is an eight-wheeled amphibious armoured personnel carrier that serves widely across the former Soviet Union and beyond.

name: BTR-82A
description: The BTR-82A modernises the BTR-80 with a 30mm autocannon, spall liners, and improved night sights.

name: Boxer
description: The Boxer uses swappable mission modules on a common 8x8 drive chassis, so one platform can serve as a troop carrier, ambulance, or command post.

name: Patria AMV
description: The Patria AMV is a modular Finnish 8x8 vehicle known for protection and off-road mobility, operated by more than ten countries.

name: Namer
description: The Namer is built on a Merkava tank chassis, which makes it one of the most heavily armoured troop carriers in the world.

name: FV432
description: The FV432 has carried British infantry since the 1960s and remains in use as a mortar carrier, ambulance, and command vehicle.

name: TPz Fuchs
description: The Fuchs is an amphibious 6x6 transport best known in NBC reconnaissance roles, detecting nuclear, biological, and chemical hazards.

name: VAB
description: The VAB (Véhicule de l'Avant Blindé) was the French Army's standard wheeled troop carrier for four decades.

name: Sd.Kfz. 251
description: The Sd.Kfz. 251 half-track carried German panzergrenadiers so they could keep pace with the tanks, and it was built in more than 20 variants.

name: M3 Half-track
description: The M3 Half-track was the main American armoured troop carrier of WWII and was supplied in large numbers to Allied forces.

name: Universal Carrier
armament: .303 Bren LMG or Boys anti-tank rifle
description: The Universal Carrier (Bren Carrier) is the most-produced armoured fighting vehicle in history, with around 113,000 built.

name: MaxxPro MRAP
description: The MaxxPro is a mine-resistant ambush-protected vehicle with a V-shaped hull that deflects blasts from roadside bombs.

name: Bushmaster PMV
description: The Bushmaster is an Australian protected mobility vehicle credited with saving many lives in Afghanistan, and it has been exported to several armies.

name: PzH 2000
description: The Panzerhaubitze 2000 can fire three rounds in under ten seconds and put several shells on one target at the same moment (MRSI).

name: K9 Thunder
description: The K9 Thunder is the world's best-selling self-propelled howitzer, operated by more than ten countries.

name: CAESAR
description: CAESAR mounts a 155mm howitzer on a 6x6 truck, so it can fire and move away within minutes and can be airlifted by a C-130.

name: 2S19 Msta-S
description: The 2S19 Msta-S is the main heavy self-propelled howitzer of the Russian Army, built on a hull that combines T-72 and T-80 components.

name: 2S3 Akatsiya
description: The 2S3 Akatsiya was the Soviet answer to the M109 and remains in service across many former Warsaw Pact armies.

name: AS-90
description: The AS-90 was the British Army's standard self-propelled gun from 1993 until it began being replaced, with many units donated to Ukraine.

name: Archer
description: Archer is a fully automated wheeled howitzer that can fire its first round within 30 seconds of stopping and be moving again moments later.

name: M7 Priest
description: The M7 Priest got its name from its pulpit-like machine-gun ring and provided mobile artillery support to Allied armoured divisions.

name: Wespe
description: The Wespe mounted a 105mm howitzer on an obsolete Panzer II chassis, giving panzer divisions mobile light artillery.

name: M142 HIMARS
armament: 6x GMLRS guided rockets or 1x ATACMS missile
description: HIMARS is a wheeled rocket launcher that fires precision-guided rockets and relocates within minutes, making it hard to counter.

name: M270 MLRS
description: The M270 is a tracked multiple rocket launcher that can saturate a large area or fire precision rockets, operated by many NATO armies.

name: BM-21 Grad
description: The BM-21 Grad is the world's most widespread multiple rocket launcher; it can fire all 40 rockets in about 20 seconds.

name: BM-13 Katyusha
description: The Katyusha rocket launcher was feared for its sudden, howling salvos. German troops nicknamed it "Stalin's organ".

name: LAV-25
description: The LAV-25 is the US Marine Corps' amphibious light armoured reconnaissance vehicle, prized for speed and range.

name: FV107 Scimitar
description: The Scimitar is a tracked reconnaissance vehicle from the CVR(T) family, used by British reconnaissance units for decades.

name: Fennek
description: The Fennek is a low-profile scout car with a mast-mounted sensor suite that can observe targets from long range while staying hidden.

name: BRDM-2
description: The BRDM-2 is an amphibious scout car with retractable belly wheels for crossing trenches, and it has been exported to dozens of countries.

name: AMX-10 RC
description: The AMX-10 RC is a six-wheeled armoured car with tank-like firepower, used for reconnaissance and fire support.

name: EBRC Jaguar
armament: 40mm CTA40 cannon, 7.62mm RWS, 2x Akeron MP missiles
description: The Jaguar replaces the AMX-10 RC as part of France's SCORPION programme, networked with other vehicles to share targets in real time.

name: Sd.Kfz. 234/2 Puma
description: The Puma was an eight-wheeled armoured car with an exceptional range for WWII and a 50mm gun that let it fight its way out of trouble.

name: M8 Greyhound
description: The M8 Greyhound was a fast six-wheeled armoured car used by US cavalry reconnaissance units in Europe and the Pacific.

name: Flakpanzer Gepard
description: The Gepard uses twin radar-guided 35mm guns on a Leopard 1 hull, and it has recently proved effective against drones and cruise missiles.

name: ZSU-23-4 Shilka
description: The Shilka pairs four radar-guided 23mm cannons, and it was feared by low-flying aircraft in Vietnam and the Middle East.

name: 2K22 Tunguska
description: The Tunguska combines guns and missiles on one tracked chassis to protect armoured columns from helicopters and aircraft.

name: Pantsir-S1
description: The Pantsir-S1 is a truck-mounted gun-missile system that provides short-range defence against aircraft, drones, and precision munitions.

name: 9K330 Tor
description: The Tor is an all-weather, short-range missile system that can detect and engage several targets while on the move.

name: AN/TWQ-1 Avenger
description: The Avenger mounts a turret with eight Stinger missiles on a Humvee to protect troops from low-flying aircraft and drones.

name: Stryker M-SHORAD
armament: 30mm XM914 cannon, Stinger and Hellfire missiles, 7.62mm MG
description: M-SHORAD restores short-range air defence to US armoured units, mounting a gun and missile turret on the Stryker chassis.

name: Flakpanzer IV Wirbelwind
description: The Wirbelwind ("Whirlwind") put a quad 20mm flak turret on a Panzer IV chassis to protect armoured units from Allied fighter-bombers.

name: M16 MGMC
description: The M16 half-track carried four .50-calibre machine guns and was nicknamed the "meat chopper" for its devastating ground-attack use.

name: Willys MB Jeep
description: The Willys MB Jeep became a WWII icon. It could carry troops, tow guns, or serve as an ambulance, and it went on to inspire civilian 4x4s.

name: Volkswagen Kübelwagen
description: The Kübelwagen was a light, air-cooled military car based on the Volkswagen Beetle; its flat underside let it slide over mud and sand.

name: HMMWV (Humvee)
description: The Humvee replaced the Jeep as the US military's light utility vehicle in the 1980s and has been built in dozens of configurations.

name: Oshkosh JLTV
description: The Joint Light Tactical Vehicle is replacing the Humvee, offering MRAP-level blast protection with far better off-road mobility.

name: GAZ Tigr
description: The GAZ Tigr is a Russian high-mobility armoured utility vehicle widely used by the army, police, and special forces.
